subject: Benchmark readout & next-step check-in
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Park <julia.park@heliosretail.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-28T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Quick recap + agreed next steps from earlier today

Hi Julia — thanks again for the time earlier today. Wanted to capture the fast summary and next actions so we’re all aligned:

- Scope we discussed: product search rerank (realtime snippets) across 4 regions, 99th pct latency target <= 180ms for single-turn queries, peak concurrent QPS ~1200.
- Redwood actions: run a focused latency/throughput bench on a representative 3B model variant, include continuous-batching and KV cache patterns to estimate p99 and cost per 1k tokens.
- Helios actions: provide a small sample production trace (anonymized) and confirm whether traffic is bursty or smooth.

I’ll attach the initial bench plan and we’ll follow with numbers by EOD Monday. If anything above is off, flag it and I’ll update the record.

Next steps:
1) I’ll send the bench readout once Monica has processed the trace.
2) We’ll propose an initial POC configuration and an internal SLO review.
3) If numbers look good, schedule a short SRE sync to line up deployment constraints.

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes | Account Executive | Redwood Inference
T: (415) 555-0123 | rafael.mendes@redwood.ai

Attachment: bench-readout-20261128.pdf

From: Julia Park <julia.park@heliosretail.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-29T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + agreed next steps from earlier today

Thanks Rafael — appreciate the recap. A couple quick questions from our side before you run the full bench: 

1) For p99 measurements, can you include a breakdown with and without KV cache warm? Our traffic pattern is bursty (holiday prep), so cold-cache p99 matters for tail behavior.
2) Can you show per-request GPU memory consumption and expected KV cache hit-rate assumptions? We have tight memory constraints on the Dedicated pools.

I’ll loop in our SRE alias if we need deeper instrumentation. Otherwise happy to take the readout when ready.

— Julia
Julia Park | Head of ML Ops | Helios Retail
julia.park@heliosretail.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Park <julia.park@heliosretail.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-30T08:21:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + agreed next steps from earlier today

On Mon, Nov 30, 2026 at 08:21 Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Julia — Monica here from Redwood’s Performance team. I ran the bench using your anonymized trace and toggled cache warm/cold, and captured GPU memory, token throughput, and p50/p95/p99 slices.
> Attached is a short summary PDF and a CSV with the raw latency matrix. Key highlights:
> - Configuration: 3B model variant, int8 quant, continuous batching target=32, KV cache on/off.
> - p99 (warm cache): 140ms 
> - p99 (cold cache): 360ms (single-node, no pre-warming)
> - Sustained throughput (per GPU): ~850 tokens/sec at target batch sizes
> - GPU memory: peak 22GB with cache warm, 20GB cold (cache adds KV state)
> - Cost estimate: ~0.9 USD per 1k tokens (hosted config), dedicated pricing will be lower with reservations
>
> I included assumptions at the top of the CSV (redwood_latency_matrix.csv) and a couple of suggested mitigations for cold-cache tail: pre-warm policies, lightweight async priming, and a fallback smaller model for very tight SLO windows.
>
> Rafael will follow up on priority and next steps.
>
Best,
Monica

Attachment: redwood_latency_matrix.csv, bench-readout-20261128.pdf

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Park <julia.park@heliosretail.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-01T09:48:00-08:00
Subject: Quick pulse — where does this sit on your priority list?

Hi Julia — just nudging this thread since we sent the readout and the SRE assumptions yesterday. Monica captured both warm and cold-cache p99s and outlined mitigations for the cold-cache tail (see attached CSV). Wanted to check a couple quick things so we can scope the POC correctly:

- Would Helios be open to a small pre-warming strategy + lightweight priming for peak windows, or do you need a no-priming solution?
- Is Dedicated reserved capacity something you’d consider for predictable tail behavior, or should we focus on hosted + fallbacks?

If this is lower priority right now, totally understand — a simple reply (e.g., “pause” or “go”) is helpful so we don’t keep pinging. If helpful, I can book a 20-min SRE sync this week and bring Monica for the deep-dive.

Thanks,
Rafael
